reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that trace O and N promote phase segregation and softening upon aging at 700°C in a TiVNbTa RHEA, but it does not involve Ti–Ni-based HEAs, grain boundary segregation, or the specific processing comparison proposed. The key premises are therefore extrapolated from a different alloy system without direct support.
premises: Interstitial impurities (O, N) promote nanoscale phase segregation at grain boundaries in Ti–Ni-based HEAs at elevated temperature
Impurity-induced segregation leads to precipitate-free zones and softening at high temperature
Reducing interstitial uptake preserves the solid-solution state and impedes dislocation motion
Ultra-high purity processing yields higher yield strength and creep resistance than standard processing
